ThingDef.label: adamantite ore
ThingDef.description: Raw adamantite ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: adamantite ingot
ThingDef.description: Adamantite is a heavy, stubborn metal mined deep under Tamriel. It is not quite adamantium, but it is close.

ThingDef.label: adamantium ore
ThingDef.description: Raw adamantium ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: adamantium ingot
ThingDef.description: Adamantium is an extremely hard, heavy metal mined in Morrowind. Adamantium armor is among the strongest in Tamriel, though few can afford its weight or price.

ThingDef.label: buoyant steel scraps
ThingDef.description: Scraps of buoyant steel, salvaged from the wrecks of Maormer and Sload ships. They need smelting down before the metal can be used.

ThingDef.label: buoyant steel ingot
ThingDef.description: Buoyant steel is an unusually light steel of the southern seas. It is said to float, which is why sailors trust their lives to it.

ThingDef.label: brass ingot
ThingDef.description: Brass is a bright alloy of copper and zinc. It is better suited to fittings and ornaments than to war.

ThingDef.label: bronze ingot
ThingDef.description: Bronze is a strong alloy of copper and tin. The Dwemer built their machines and armor from metals like it, and their work still outlasts most steel.

ThingDef.label: cobalt ore
ThingDef.description: Raw cobalt ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: cobalt ingot
ThingDef.description: Cobalt is a hard blue-gray metal. Dunmer smiths sometimes use it for fittings and armor plate.

ThingDef.label: copper ore
ThingDef.description: Raw copper ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: copper ingot
ThingDef.description: Copper is soft and easily worked. It is too weak for good arms on its own, but it alloys with tin into bronze and with zinc into brass.

ThingDef.label: corundum ore
ThingDef.description: Raw corundum ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: corundum ingot
ThingDef.description: Corundum is a hard, reddish metal. On its own it makes middling arms. Smiths mostly alloy it with iron to make steel, as the Nords and the Dwemer did.

ThingDef.label: ebony ore
ThingDef.description: Raw ebony ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: ebony ingot
ThingDef.description: Ebony is a dark, glassy metal said to be the blood of a dead god. It is very rare, very heavy and very strong, and only daedric arms surpass it.

ThingDef.label: malachite ore
ThingDef.description: Raw malachite ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: refined malachite
ThingDef.description: Refined malachite is the light, glassy green metal of glass arms and armor. It is light as elven gear and keeps a vicious edge.

ThingDef.label: iron ore
ThingDef.description: Raw iron ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: iron ingot
ThingDef.description: Iron is the common metal of Tamriel, worked into the plain arms and armor of every militia and bandit camp. Smelted with corundum, it makes steel.

ThingDef.label: meteoric iron ore
ThingDef.description: Raw meteoric iron ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: meteoric iron ingot
ThingDef.description: Meteoric iron falls from the sky inside shooting stars. The Ayleids prized it, and blades forged from it are said to cut true.

ThingDef.label: mithril ore
ThingDef.description: Raw mithril ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: mithril ingot
ThingDef.description: Mithril is a light, silvery metal with an elven look to it. Mithril armor is nearly as strong as steel at half the weight.

ThingDef.label: moonstone ore
ThingDef.description: Raw moonstone ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: moonstone ingot
ThingDef.description: Refined moonstone is the pale, light metal of elven arms and armor. It is not as strong as orichalcum, but it is far lighter and turns heat well.

ThingDef.label: nickel ore
ThingDef.description: Raw nickel ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: nickel ingot
ThingDef.description: Nickel is a hard, pale metal used in coins and fittings. It makes passable arms at best.

ThingDef.label: orgnium ore
ThingDef.description: Raw orgnium ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: orgnium ingot
ThingDef.description: Orgnium is a rare green-black metal from the far corners of Tamriel. It takes a fine edge and resists heat.

ThingDef.label: orichalcum ore
ThingDef.description: Raw orichalcum ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: orichalcum ingot
ThingDef.description: Orichalcum is a dense green metal that Orsimer smiths work into heavy orcish arms and armor. It is tougher than steel, and heavier.

ThingDef.label: palladium ore
ThingDef.description: Raw palladium ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: palladium ingot
ThingDef.description: Palladium is a rare, lustrous precious metal. It is far too soft for war, but jewelers and nobles pay well for it.

ThingDef.label: quicksilver ore
ThingDef.description: Raw quicksilver ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: quicksilver ingot
ThingDef.description: Quicksilver is a bright, light metal. Altmer smiths alloy it with refined moonstone to make elven arms and armor.

ThingDef.label: tin ore
ThingDef.description: Raw tin ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: tin ingot
ThingDef.description: Tin is soft and dull. Nobody fights with it, but smiths alloy it with copper to make bronze.

ThingDef.label: zinc ore
ThingDef.description: Raw zinc ore, dug from the rock. It has to be smelted into ingots before it can be worked.

ThingDef.label: zinc ingot
ThingDef.description: Zinc is brittle and gray. Nobody fights with it, but smiths alloy it with copper to make brass.

ThingDef.label: stalhrim
ThingDef.description: Stalhrim is enchanted ice found only in the coldest places of Tamriel, such as the far north of Solstheim. It never melts and is worked raw rather than smelted. Stalhrim arms and armor are lighter than ebony and nearly as strong, and they bite with the cold.

ThingDef.label: heart stone
ThingDef.description: A dark crystal that still pulses faintly with the power of the Heart of Lorkhan. Alchemists and enchanters pay well for them.

ThingDef.label: bones
ThingDef.description: Bones taken from a butchered animal. Ground up and bound with resin, they make bonemold.

ThingDef.label: fat
ThingDef.description: Animal fat cut away during butchering. It burns slowly and cleanly, and fuels iron lanterns.

ThingDef.label: chitin
ThingDef.description: Plates of chitin cut from the shells of giant insects. Light and tough, it works like wood or bone and makes good armor.

ThingDef.label: bonemold
ThingDef.description: Ground bone mixed with a sticky resin. Light and durable once it sets, it is the Dunmer's favorite armoring material. Most likely they took to it because bone was easier to come by than wood or iron, while ebony and glass were kept for the wealthy.

ThingDef.label: bonemold blocks
ThingDef.description: Blocks of bonemold. Roughly on par with sandstone blocks, but lighter and less durable.

ThingDef.label: fire salts
ThingDef.description: Fire salts are the glowing remains of a slain flame atronach, and they stay warm long after the atronach is gone. A handful burns far longer than wood, so smiths prize them as fuel for forges and smelters.

ThingDef.label: frost salts
ThingDef.description: Frost salts are the crystalline remains of a slain frost atronach, cold enough to numb the fingers. Alchemists across Tamriel pay well for them.

ThingDef.label: void salts
ThingDef.description: Void salts are the dark, crackling remains of a slain storm atronach. They are rare, and alchemists and enchanters pay a great deal for them.

ThingDef.label: ash salts
ThingDef.description: Ash salts are gathered from the ash of Red Mountain and the creatures that live in it. The healers of Morrowind trade for them to fight the blight.
